headline: All majors below the 200-day line, long liquidations dwarf shorts, but whales are moving coins off exchange into cold storage.
paragraphs: The regime is one: seven of seven assets trade below their 200-day simple moving averages, and none have completed a golden cross. Bitcoin sits 49.9 percent below its 12-month high of 124,739.81, Ethereum off 61.5 percent from 4,817.76, and Solana down 70.6 percent from 247.60. There is no disagreement in the major trend lines. The market is in a downtrend by structure, and the bounce zones (90-day ranges shown in the price sparklines) are the floor: Bitcoin has traded between 58,566.09 and 82,018.37 over that window; Ethereum between 1,566.01 and 2,369.96; Solana between 62.18 and 97.25. Prices near the lows of those ranges tell you the market is testing support, not rolling over into new lows.

Momentum is mixed and that matters. Bitcoin's RSI-14 sits at 42.6 and its MACD is below its signal line, the setup of a still-resting downtrend. Ethereum at 50.5 RSI with MACD below signal is neutral bordering on tired. But Solana at 41.5 RSI, XRP at 40.8, and Doge at 38.0 are all in oversold territory (below 40), yet their MACD lines remain below signal, meaning the bounce, if it comes, has not yet found directional conviction. BNB and Doge are the two exceptions: both show MACD above signal line despite prices still below the 200-day. That is a divergence, a whisper that momentum may be decoupling from the downtrend, though both assets still sit underwater on the 12-month (BNB down 55.3 percent, Doge down 76.1 percent). The take: oversold RSI without upside momentum confirmation is not capitulation yet, it is exhaustion pausing.

Positioning in perpetual futures reveals acute stress on the long side. Bitcoin funding over the last eight hours is 0.0079 percent (annualizing to 8.7 percent), Ethereum at 0.0016 percent annualized to 1.7 percent. Those rates are positive, meaning long holders are still paying shorts to hold their bets, but Bitcoin's annual rate is material and XRP is at 0.0084 percent (9.1 annualized), the most expensive short squeeze insurance on the board. More urgent: over the last 21 hours, Bitcoin saw 1,595 liquidations with 12.4 million in longs wiped out against only 787 thousand in shorts. Ethereum over 18 hours had 1,600 liquidations, 15.4 million longs versus 1.1 million shorts. Solana, XRP, and Doge all show similar imbalance, liquidations running 9 to 10 times higher on the long side than the short side. Open interest across the majors remains substantial: Bitcoin at 2 billion, Ethereum at 1.4 billion, Solana at 214 million. The long positioning is crowded and the wicks are being tested.

Whale behavior offers a counterweight to that pain. Over the past 24 hours, Bitcoin saw a net 58.5 million dollars move off exchanges, split between 110.4 million flowing onto venues (Coinbase Institutional taking 55.5 million, Binance taking 54.9 million) and 168.9 million flowing off (Kraken sending out 116.8 million). The net off-exchange move is a signal: when liquidations are firing and prices are testing the low end of the range, whales moving coins to cold storage is a read of accumulation on dips, not panic selling into rallies. Stablecoin float stands at 303.8 billion, down 1.62 percent over the month, a slow bleed. Over the past four weeks the whale weekly net has swung: plus 918 million, minus 185 million, minus 104 million, then plus 1.3 billion last week. That volatility means no single trend, but the most recent week showed strong net inflow into wallets. Stablecoin buying power attached to whales is negative 152 million, which means more stablecoins are moving off exchange than onto it, tightening the dry powder pool even as coins are being held in cold storage.

The Fear and Greed index reads 25, extreme fear, on a 30-day range of 19 to 33. That range is tight and stays in extreme territory, meaning the crowd has been scared for a while without relief. The contradiction is surgical: the tape shows long liquidations and oversold momentum, yet whales are quietly moving coins off exchange and the weekly flow turned sharply positive in the most recent session. Sentiment is trapped in the lows; positioning shows pain; structure shows support being tested. Bitcoin dominance is 56.1 percent, market cap off 2.43 percent on the day, the moves in line with a down day in the majors. Fees on the Bitcoin network are at their lowest (three satoshis per byte), and difficulty is down 2.0 percent with a retarget 1,215 blocks away, suggesting miners are winding down against the margin pressure.

Watch three conditions to read the tape as it moves: whether whale weekly net inflows reverse into outflow (the most recent week's inflow was strong; the prior three were mixed to negative), whether Bitcoin reclaims above the 200-day SMA and whether that coincides with a MACD turn back above signal line (the setup for a golden cross), and whether long liquidations stabilize below the 10-to-1 ratio on shorts or spike higher (a spike suggests capitulation is still incomplete). The floor is being tested by price; the pain is being felt in long portfolios; and the whales are buying it. What happens next depends on whether that buying becomes conviction or a trap door.
